This is therefore a reinsurance (retrocession) contract.

Because the agreement contains all principal terms of the risk transfer – the parties, the scope of the ceded business, the quota‑share nature, consideration, and operative clauses – it constitutes a main contract rather than a mere amendment or endorsement.

The cession is for the entirety of the identified contracts (100 % quota share), indicating an obligatory arrangement where the ceding insurers must transfer the risk. Hence the contract is obligatory.

The agreement explicitly states the reinsurance is on a “100 % quota share basis,” which is a classic proportional reinsurance structure.

The underlying policies mentioned are “crop hail policies,” which are property insurance lines, i.e., non‑life coverage.

Accordingly, the class of business is Property (agricultural/property).
